newsitem.title: CANADA: Coastal, Westcoast seen set for gas merger.
newsitem.headline: Coastal, Westcoast seen set for gas merger.

text.p: Houston-based Coastal Corp and Westcoast Energy Inc of Vancouver appear close to announcing a deal to merge their natural gas marketing divisions in a move that would create North America's fourth largest marketing operation, industry sources say.

"It is going ahead," said an informed source who spoke on condition of anonymity. "The impression that they're trying to give people is that it's being discussed, when it's being discussed with a view to completion."
The move would follow recent similar gas megamergers, including those by NGC Corp and Chevron Corp, as well as PanEnergy Corp and Mobil Corp.
Together, the combined entity would manage about 6.7 billion cubic feet of gas per day.
Spokespeople from Westcoast and Coastal declined to comment on the deal's progress.
"It's an industry trend," said Coastal spokesman Brian Mitchell. "But as far as this particular report, I can't add anything to it."
"I really have to decline commenting at this stage," said Westcoast's Patricia Bowles.
Westcoast, Canada's third largest integrated pipeline and gas marketing company, operates British Columbia's gas gathering and transport systems and owns the gas utilities Centra and Union Gas.

Westcoast's gas marketing arm, Westcoast Gas Services, provides merchant sales and trading, risk management services, gas supply management and structured financing at nine offices across North America. Its main office is in Calgary.
In 1995, Westcoast Gas, which moves an average of 3.2 billion cubic feet a day, lost C$1 million.
One Canadian pipeline analyst said Westcoast, faced with intense and growing competition in gas marketing, was at a point where it had to decide to get much larger or leave the sector.

"(There's been) a lack of earnings capability to date, partly due to depressed gas pricing in B.C.," said ScotiaMcleod's Sam Kanes. "They should get bigger or get out and taking a smaller percentage of something bigger makes sense."

Westcoast Energy said in August it was restructuring its pipeline and field services divisions in an effort to lower costs. Its gas marketing arm was also smarting this week from the defection to a U.S.-based company of four of its top natural gas traders from the Calgary office.
Coastal Gas Marketing, a unit of integrated oil and gas company Coastal Corp, is the eighth largest gas marketing company in the United States, moving an average of 3.5 billion cubic feet a day.

The unit also has a Calgary office, but it is much smaller than Canada's heavyweights, which include Westcoast, TransCanada PipeLines Ltd marketing arm TransCanada Gas Services, and Novagas Clearinghouse Ltd, owned by NOVA Corp and NGC Corp.
Both parent companies hold a 50 percent stake in the Empire State Pipeline in the U.S. Northeast.
Carol Coale, natural gas analyst with Prudential Securities in Houston, said the trend to megamarketers had grown as companies found the need to cover the largest market area for the lowest cost.
"Unless you have a small, focused effort, you really have to play the market share game," Coale said, adding that Coastal's marketing arm had been an underperformer.
"To be a low-cost provider, you've got to run enough volumes through your system to make it worthwhile," she said.
The largest gas marketers in North America are NGC-Chevron, Enron Corp and Mobil-PanEnergy.
Westcoast was down 0.15 to 21.50 in late trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange. Coastal was off 3/8 to 39-5/8 on the New York Stock Exchange.
-- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
